title: A Skid Steer Controller That Knows Slip: The Track It Really Turns On, the Speed the Ground Allows in a Turn, and Why the Plain Follower Slides Wide

questions.question: Why does a skid steer vehicle turn less than the plain track geometry says?
options: The wheels slide sideways: the effective track is chi times the real one

questions.question: Holding the path on tarmac: aware against unaware, the worst error was:
questions.explanation: The unaware one asks for a turn that is too small.

questions.question: On ice at 1.2 m/s the plain controller let go in how many steps?
questions.explanation: The speed was above what the grip holds.

questions.question: How many times the speed does the same curve allow on gravel than on ice?
questions.explanation: The square root of the ratio of mu.

questions.question: What does the limited controller give up?
options: Time: 5.4 s against 4.6 s on ice
questions.explanation: It is slower and on the path.

questions.question: Why is there a floor on the speed in a turn?
options: A controller that can command zero in a turn never gets out of it
questions.explanation: A vehicle that stops is not following.
